comparator.sourceNotes: Assess only the independently prescribed60EC common firstyear. Retain all25supported components174EC; exclude114listed laterEC and6unlistedQuantumPhysics. Required54EC Materials track is expanded once into48supported plus6access-unreconciledEC. CurrentQuantum restriction, all project/safety/120EC/firstyear conditions and30genuine open remain unwaived. components.name: Engineering the Building Blocks of Life
Design Project
components.note: A compulsory team project follows the selected specialisation. Workshops and preparation run throughout the year, with execution in the final period. Practical participation requires the programme’s safety instruction.

components.name: Advanced Ethical Prototyping
components.note: A full-time eight-week team project develops a physical prototype through design, testing and ethical decisions. It ends with a demonstration, presentation and a partly individual defence. Entry requires the completed first year, at least 120 EC and the Design Project; practical work requires safety instruction.

components.name: Bachelor Project Science, Technology & Innovation
components.note: An individual supervised research project includes a thesis and presentation and is examined by at least two UvA examiners. Entry requires the completed first year, at least 120 EC and the Design Project. External projects need Examination Board permission.

components.name: Open elective space
components.note: Thirty EC remain open for electives or a minor, normally in the first semester of year three. The study plan is assessed for overlap and approval; at most 12 EC may be introductory subjects, and a foreign minor needs prior approval.

comparisonAlignment.rationale: Both directly study waves and physical measurement, including optical/spectral interpretation. ST&I additionally introduces Schrodinger/particle-in-box and atomic quantum theory not supplied by this UCR course.

Both directly assess sustainable-energy technologies and their technical performance. UCR emphasises usage/system/economic assessment; ST&I additionally develops chemical bonding, reaction thermodynamics/kinetics and fuel-conversion laboratories.
Both develop programming, algorithms and computational problem solving for models. Scientific contexts and breadth of simulation work differ.
Both develop calculus/differential-equation and computational tools for scientific models. ST&I contextualises its4EC across four themes; UCR uses a dynamic-model project.
Both directly develop matrices, eigenvalues and linear-system computation. ST&I additionally integrates multivariable calculus, statistics and combinatorics across themes.
Both investigate motion/kinematics for physical technological systems. UCR programs robotic manipulation; full Newtonian force/conservation, drones/gyroscopes and the ST&I Makerspace build differ.
Both directly develop databases and querying. UCR does not supply the full JavaScript/client-server/web-interface sequence.

Both study molecular/cellular structure, proteins, membranes, genome expression and bioenergetics. UCR emphasises cellular mechanisms and research interpretation; the full ST&I microscopy/computational practical differs.
Both use molecular cloning/transformation, PCR and DNA/protein laboratory investigation. ST&I additionally teaches specific CRISPR/Gibson/sequencing and synthetic-toggle methods not established here.

Both use design thinking and project development toward a technological product. UCR prototypes are developed where feasible; no RaspberryPi, 3D-printing, soldering or compulsory Makerspace sequence is inferred.

The selected geochemistry/lifecycle courses are relevant to technologies, but do not directly teach the integrated plant/agrochemical/farm food-production object. No relationship is forced from generic chemical-analysis methods.
PPD supports academic inquiry and reflection, but those transferable skills do not establish a close relationship to this integrated technical Makerspace/microcontroller formation.

comparator.note: A compulsory team project follows the selected specialisation. Workshops and preparation run throughout the year, with execution in the final period. Practical participation requires the programme’s safety instruction.

A full-time eight-week team project develops a physical prototype through design, testing and ethical decisions. It ends with a demonstration, presentation and a partly individual defence. Entry requires the completed first year, at least 120 EC and the Design Project; practical work requires safety instruction.

An individual supervised research project includes a thesis and presentation and is examined by at least two UvA examiners. Entry requires the completed first year, at least 120 EC and the Design Project. External projects need Examination Board permission.

Thirty EC remain open for electives or a minor, normally in the first semester of year three. The study plan is assessed for overlap and approval; at most 12 EC may be introductory subjects, and a foreign minor needs prior approval.

notes.text: The confirmed common first year combines natural science, computing, quantitative methods and technology design. UCR offers broader material/living-system, digital/robotic and biological-health responses. Quantum and optical theory, chemical energy laboratories, advanced genome-engineering, web technologies and the sustained Makerspace fabrication and microcontroller sequence remain differences within that core. All later specialisation, final projects and full progression are excluded.

audience.programmeDescription: Science, Technology & Innovation at the University of Amsterdam is a Dutch-taught programme combining natural sciences, data and modelling with the design and testing of technological prototypes. This example follows High-tech Designer Materials.
audience.comparisonExplanation: This qualified comparison assesses the confirmed 60 EC common first year of Science, Technology & Innovation. The three UCR programmes develop different combinations of material and biological science, computation, laboratory inquiry and technological design. They do not reproduce all physics, chemical energy, synthetic biology, web technology or sustained Makerspace fabrication and microcontroller training. All later specialisation, projects, final research and complete progression are excluded.

curriculum.limitation: All 25 documented components/174 EC remain visible, including 30 EC genuine open space without chosen contents. Only the 60 EC common first year is assessed. All 114 listed laterEC and the 6 EC QuantumPhysics requirement are excluded. QuantumPhysics access and a complete 180 EC route remain unverified; no specialist or graduation eligibility is certified.

componentNotes.y1-58719: Builds mathematical, statistical and computational foundations and applies them to the programme’s scientific themes.
componentNotes.y1-61760: Studies food systems through nutrient and carbon cycles, agricultural chemistry, farm fieldwork, soil analysis and ethical and social questions.
componentNotes.y1-58696: Introduces computational thinking, algorithms and programming for scientific modelling and simulation.
componentNotes.y1-58958: Develops academic practices, teamwork and design skills, with workshops, a reflective portfolio and practical technical activities.
componentNotes.y1-59419: Introduces cellular building blocks, biochemistry and molecular processes, using microscopy and computational models.
componentNotes.y1-58679: Applies Newtonian mechanics to moving objects and a practical design-and-build task in the Makerspace.
componentNotes.y1-58798: Continues mathematical, statistical and computational skills in the context of second-semester scientific themes.
componentNotes.y1-58951: Develops client-server applications, databases, data cleaning and querying, and interactive web content using JavaScript.
componentNotes.y1-59418: Develops molecular cloning, genome-engineering and bioinformatics techniques through laboratory and computational work.
componentNotes.y1-58768: Continues academic practices, teamwork and technical development through workshops and reflective work.
componentNotes.y1-58799: Studies waves, oscillations, light and their interaction with matter, including the foundations of sensors and optical instruments.
componentNotes.y1-58702: Connects chemical bonding, thermodynamics and reaction kinetics to energy conversion, storage and practical energy technologies.
componentNotes.y2-58706: A compulsory team project follows the selected specialisation. Workshops and preparation run throughout the year, with execution in the final period. Practical participation requires the programme’s safety instruction. This component is outside the assessed 60 EC common first year.
componentNotes.y2-59420: Introduces bonding, crystal structure and electronic behaviour in condensed-matter and materials physics. This component is outside the assessed 60 EC common first year.
componentNotes.y2-58586: Develops vector calculus, eigenvalue methods, complex matrices and systems of differential equations for scientific modelling. This component is outside the assessed 60 EC common first year.
componentNotes.y2-58874: Applies machine learning to scientific problems, including computational representations of molecules and materials. This component is outside the assessed 60 EC common first year.
componentNotes.y2-58521: Combines electronics and photonics with circuit construction, simulation, measurements, filters and spectroscopy. This component is outside the assessed 60 EC common first year.
componentNotes.y2-58760: Develops statistical data analysis and Python programming using a realistic dataset. This component is outside the assessed 60 EC common first year.
componentNotes.y2-59430: Studies fluid and solid mechanics, viscosity, elasticity and viscoelastic behaviour across microscopic and macroscopic scales. This component is outside the assessed 60 EC common first year.
componentNotes.y2-58591: Examines telescopes, microscopes and detectors, linking optical and detector technology to scientific discovery and measurement. This component is outside the assessed 60 EC common first year.
componentNotes.y2-61794: Uses statistical thermodynamics to connect molecular behaviour to material properties, phase transitions and soft-matter systems. This component is outside the assessed 60 EC common first year.
componentNotes.y2-58830: Applies thermodynamics, quantum mechanics and electromagnetism to energy conversion and storage, including semiconductors and batteries. This component is outside the assessed 60 EC common first year.
componentNotes.y3-59335: A full-time eight-week team project develops a physical prototype through design, testing and ethical decisions. It ends with a demonstration, presentation and a partly individual defence. Entry requires the completed first year, at least 120 EC and the Design Project; practical work requires safety instruction. This component is outside the assessed 60 EC common first year.
componentNotes.y3-59417: An individual supervised research project includes a thesis and presentation and is examined by at least two UvA examiners. Entry requires the completed first year, at least 120 EC and the Design Project. External projects need Examination Board permission. This component is outside the assessed 60 EC common first year.
componentNotes.y3-open: Thirty EC remain open for electives or a minor, normally in the first semester of year three. The study plan is assessed for overlap and approval; at most 12 EC may be introductory subjects, and a foreign minor needs prior approval. This component is outside the assessed 60 EC common first year.
